group.passage:
Most of us have physical imperfections we dislike, be it an uneven smile, a flat nose, or crooked teeth. Regardless of how we feel about our defects, they do not interfere with our daily lives. However, for those who suffer from body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), the defects often cause severe emotional distress and difficulties in daily functioning. Patients with BDD may spend hours each day focusing on their flaws, unable to restrain their negative thoughts and constantly comparing their appearances to those of others. Instead of trusting people who tell them how good they look, they tend to put a lot of energy into concealing flaws, such as spending a long time combing their hair, applying make-up, or choosing clothes that highlight their best features. The anxiety that people will notice their shortcomings may cause them to skip work or school, avoid social situations, and even isolate themselves from family and friends.
According to the study, BDD is mostly diagnosed in adolescents aged 12 to 13, and it affects men and women almost equally in the United States. The causes of BDD are unknown, but biological and environmental factors, including a family history of BDD, negative self-image, abnormal brain function, and low levels of serotonin, may all play a role. In order to ease the uncomfortable feelings that are caused by BDD, cognitive behavioral therapy is commonly used. It involves identifying, analyzing, and reshaping irrational thoughts into more rational self-talk. Dance and movement therapy can also assist in developing a healthy sense of trust and appreciation for one’s body. With medication and appropriate treatment, individuals with BDD can achieve significant improvement in their symptoms and quality of life.

questions.stem: What is the best title of the passage?

options.A: Treatments for Body Dysmorphic Disorder: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Medication.
options.B: The Negative Impact of Body Dysmorphic Disorder on Daily Functioning.
options.C: Body Dysmorphic Disorder: A Mental Health Condition Embracing Physical Imperfections.
options.D: Understanding the Causes, Symptoms and Treatment of Body Dysmorphic Disorder.

questions.stem: Which of the following individuals is most likely to be a BDD patient?

options.A: Mark becomes obsessed with his thinning hairline, spending significant time concealing it, feeling inadequate, and limiting his activities.
options.B: Tom stores waste at home, which creates a breeding ground for cockroaches, causing neighbors to complain and react in a negative way.
options.C: In spite of receiving a 95 on the exam, May felt unsatisfied with the results, and she still felt that she had to work harder.
options.D: Sarah regularly consumes large amounts of alcohol throughout the day, neglects her responsibilities at work and frequently gets into conflicts with her family.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: BDD is a fictional disease invented by the cosmetics industry to sell more beauty products and treatments.
options.B: BDD is a chronic disease, and there is no satisfactory treatment for it.
options.C: Female adults are more likely to suffer from BDD than male adolescents.
options.D: If one of the parents is a BDD patient, the children may suffer from the same disorder as well.

questions.stem: Which of the following may NOT be included in the BDD treatment, based on the information provided?

options.A: Group Movement Activities: Participating in cooperative movement activities, such as group dances, to improve self-acceptance.
options.B: Sleep Medications: Taking sleeping pills to eliminate chaotic thoughts and depression, seeking peace in the dream world.
options.C: Thought Record Apps: Mobile apps that help track negative thoughts about appearance and provide guidance for reframing them.
options.D: Outdoor Adventure Therapy: Engaging in outdoor activities, such as mountain climbing, to promote a positive connection with one’s body.
